demonstration_summary.title: ${var.title} complete
demonstration_summary.summary: The walkthrough answered “${scenario.title}” without changing the supplied dashboard. It applied one shared ${var.field} context, isolated the panel value representing ${truth.finding}, and then opened the supporting data to verify that the visual pattern really describes ${truth.scope}.

checks.title: Shared context
checks.detail: The dashboard’s global ${var.field} control was set to ${truth.finding}, causing every panel to refresh under the same investigation context. Using one shared filter prevented different panels from silently describing different populations or time scopes.

checks.title: Decisive panel
checks.detail: The chart value or legend series for ${truth.finding} was selected in view-only mode. This separated the abnormal segment from blended totals and made its relationship to ${truth.scope} visible without editing or resaving the dashboard.

checks.title: Underlying evidence
checks.detail: The decisive panel’s underlying data or inspection view was opened with its filters and time range intact. The source records or calculation matched the selected visual pattern, confirming that the aggregate means what the proposed conclusion claims.

demonstration_summary.evidence: The dashboard panel supplied the aggregate signal, while its preserved underlying data supplied independent support for how that signal was calculated and scoped. Both layers connect ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}, so the interpretation does not depend on the appearance of one chart alone.
demonstration_summary.conclusion: ${truth.conclusion} The selected panel establishes the visible pattern, and the underlying records corroborate that pattern under the same dashboard context.

answer.evidence: The dashboard value and underlying records connect ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Narrow the supplied dashboard
goals.concept: Global time, filters, and controls apply context across panels.
goals.narration: Narrow the dashboard to the relevant interval and scope.
goals.reasoning: A shared context makes panel comparisons meaningful.
goals.evidence: The dashboard refreshes with the narrowed state.

demonstration.narration: Use the dashboard’s global ${var.field} control to narrow “${scenario.title}” to ${truth.finding}. A global control applies the same investigation context to every panel at once.
demonstration.reasoning: Comparing panels is only meaningful when they share the same time and filter state. This removes unrelated data and ensures every chart is describing the same scope, ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.evidence: All panels should refresh and retain the ${var.field} selection for ${truth.finding}. This confirms the shared context; the decisive panel still needs to show the actual pattern.

goals.title: Interact with the decisive panel
goals.concept: Legend and value interactions can isolate a series without editing the dashboard.
goals.narration: Select the panel value that represents the abnormal segment.
goals.reasoning: The selected series identifies the scope of impact.
goals.evidence: The dashboard retains the selected value as investigation context.

demonstration.narration: Select the chart value or legend series representing ${truth.finding}. This isolates the abnormal segment in the panel while keeping the supplied dashboard in view-only mode.
demonstration.reasoning: A total or blended chart can hide which segment drives the change. Selecting this value makes the affected portion explicit and lets the other panels respond within the same ${truth.scope} context.
demonstration.evidence: The panel should visibly retain or highlight ${truth.finding}, and the dashboard should preserve that selection as investigation context. This is the aggregate signal behind “${truth.conclusion}”

goals.title: Open supporting panel evidence
goals.concept: Inspection and drilldowns explain calculation scope and connect aggregates to records.
goals.narration: Inspect the panel or open its underlying data with context intact.
goals.reasoning: This verifies that the chart means what the conclusion claims.
goals.evidence: The underlying or inspection view contains corroborating evidence.

demonstration.narration: Open the decisive panel’s underlying data or inspection view, keeping its filters and time range intact. We expect source records or calculation details that connect ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.reasoning: A chart is an aggregate and can be misread if its formula, bucket, or filters are misunderstood. Inspecting the source verifies that the visual pattern means what our proposed conclusion claims.
demonstration.evidence: The underlying view should contain records or calculations that corroborate the selected panel value. The aggregate and its source can then jointly support: ${truth.conclusion}
